solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Observer of booby and American warbler?

parts.note: a booby is a fool, as is a twit
Cher is an American singer, a warbler in the songbird sense

explanation.surface: Someone watching a seabird called the booby and a small songbird from America.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all birdwatching, with booby and warbler as birds, but booby is a fool and the warbler is the singer Cher.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitcher is a keen birdwatcher, someone who observes rare birds and travels to see them.

clue.text: They press suits and fringes of woolly jumpers

indicators.note: fringes are the edges, so only the outer parts of the phrase woolly jumpers are kept and its middle is dropped

explanation.surface: Dry-cleaners who press suits and also tidy the frayed edges of knitted sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press suits' looks like ironing, but it means pressing one's suit as a lover. The fringes here are three letters at each end: the middle LLYJUMP goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitors pressing their suit, courting a beloved, are those who woo.

clue.text: Rows of headless bodies

indicators.note: headless means the first letter of the slang word for corpses is cut off

parts.note: stiffs is slang for corpses

explanation.surface: Lines of decapitated corpses, a grim horror-film scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' reads as lines, but it is the quarrels sense, rhyming with cows.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffs are petty quarrels, and rows (said like 'cows') are arguments.

clue.text: Frightful creature heard staggerin' round raised marshland

indicators.note: round means the limping word is placed around the other piece
heard means the limping word is taken by its sound, spelt with a single B

parts.note: staggering, with the final G dropped in dialect, is hobblin'

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word for marshland is read upwards

parts.note: a bog is marshland

explanation.surface: A scary monster lurches, dialect-style, around some high moorland bog.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in staggerin' marks a dropped G, a dialect form; 'heard' says to take the word by sound, so the doubled B counts once.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobgoblin is a mischievous imp or bogey, a frightening creature of folklore.

clue.text: Mechanical ear's covered by fleece

indicators.note: in a down clue, being covered by means having the other piece placed on top

parts.note: to fleece someone is to rob them
otic means relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A mechanical ear muffled under a woolly fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic describes movement or behaviour that is machine-like, without human feeling.

clue.text: Fine American novelist ultimately very insubstantial

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
Philip Roth was an American novelist

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word very

explanation.surface: A literary verdict: a fine American novelist whose work is, in the end, rather lightweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something frothy is light and lacking substance, like foam.

clue.text: Female antelope raised on island plants

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the antelope word is read upwards

parts.note: the gnu is an African antelope

explanation.surface: A doe antelope brought up on an island among its plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Fungi are classed as plants in older and everyday usage, which the setter relies on.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms and toadstools were traditionally grouped with vegetation, so fungi count as plants loosely.

clue.text: Fulham, in the morning, work out away from main training area

indicators.note: out here means the work word lies outside the other pieces

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially a musical composition
FFC is short for Fulham Football Club, a London football club
AM means in the morning

explanation.surface: Fulham footballers do a morning workout away from their usual training ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work out' reads as exercise, but 'out' is the container signal. Fulham is a London football club, so FC (Football Club) comes with its F.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-campus means away from the university or college grounds where teaching takes place.

clue.text: Thicket where dog got tangled

indicators.note: got tangled says the letters of where dog are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A spot of undergrowth where a dog has become caught up.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedgerow is a line of bushes and shrubs, a kind of thicket bordering a field.

clue.text: Tory having great chat

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory
fab, short for fabulous, means great

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician enjoying a really good conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: A confab is an informal conversation, short for confabulation.

clue.text: A tailless dog getting stuck into its food — for real

indicators.note: getting stuck into means going inside the other piece

parts.note: a dog's food is a bone
taken as written

indicators.note: tailless means the dog's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Fido is a traditional name for a pet dog

explanation.surface: A dog with no tail tucks eagerly into its dinner, and it's genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to the dog, which is why a bone is the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Bona fide is Latin for 'in good faith', meaning genuine or real.

clue.text: Score through centre away from home

parts.note: in football, to centre the ball is to cross it into the middle
out means not at home

explanation.surface: A football report: a cross from the wing leads to a goal in an away match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' and 'centre' suggest football, but score means mark with a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To score through text is to draw a line across it, deleting it.

clue.text: Times goes after setter's pictures

indicators.note: goes after says the times word follows the setter piece

parts.note: the setter is I, so setter's is I'M, short for I am
ages means long periods of time

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper chases the crossword setter's photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Images are pictures or likenesses, whether painted, photographed or imagined.

clue.text: Apricot lover evolved into predator long ago

indicators.note: evolved means the letters of apricot lover have developed into a new form

explanation.surface: A creature fond of apricots changed over time into a carnivore in prehistoric times.
explanation.definitionFit: The velociraptor was a small, fast carnivorous dinosaur, a hunter of the distant past.

clue.text: Centre ville mistranslated — not the French for this circulatory centre

indicators.note: mistranslated says the letters of centre ville are rendered wrongly, reshuffled

parts.note: le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A sign reading 'centre ville' badly rendered, ignoring its French article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' signals taking the French article's letters away from the pool before 'mistranslated' shuffles what remains; 'this' makes the definition point at the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventricle is one of the heart's pumping chambers, a hub of blood circulation.

clue.text: Tarty live broadcast like Big Brother?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered abroad, so the letters of tarty live are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A trashy live transmission, of the sort Big Brother was known for.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Brother is a TV show where contestants live in a house under constant filming.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Brother is an example of unscripted programming that films ordinary people.

clue.text: A woman ace presiding over stunts, say?

definitions.text: A woman ace presiding over stunts, say?

indicators.note: presiding over in a down clue means sitting on top of the following piece

parts.note: taken as written
Vi is a short woman's name
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: say signals a word that matches in sound but is spelt differently

parts.note: tricks are stunts

explanation.surface: A female flying ace directing aerobatic displays.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer too: a woman pilot doing aerial stunts.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviatrix is a female pilot, so a woman ace performing aerobatic stunts.

clue.text: Form of education reducing social barriers?

definitions.text: Form of education reducing social barriers?

parts.words: Form of education reducing social barriers?
parts.note: adult tuition after work, read cryptically as levelling out the classes of society

explanation.surface: A description of schooling that breaks down divisions between rich and poor.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'evening' as making level and 'class' as social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult courses held after working hours, punningly a levelling of social strata.

clue.text: Tea Party vehicle

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
a riot is a wild party or great fun

explanation.surface: The US Tea Party movement's campaign transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a horse-drawn wheeled carriage, an ancient form of transport.

clue.text: For audience to be shown the devil is dramatic

indicators.note: for an audience means as listeners would hear it

parts.note: seen means shown; Old Nick is a name for the devil

explanation.surface: A theatre note: showing the devil to the audience makes for good drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenic can mean relating to the stage or theatrical scenery, hence dramatic.

clue.text: Sea creature spotted around site of net heading west

indicators.note: heading west in an across clue means reading from right to left
around means the spotted word goes round the other piece

parts.note: spotted means saw
a URL is the address of a site on the internet

explanation.surface: A sea creature seen near where a fishing net is, swimming westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'site of net' suggests fishing, but it is a web address. The container gives SURLAW, which 'heading west' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A walrus is a large tusked marine mammal of Arctic seas.

clue.text: South getting icy blast

parts.note: icy means cold

explanation.surface: A weather report: the south gets a freezing wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blast' looks like a gust of wind, but it is the verb meaning criticise fiercely.
explanation.definitionFit: To blast someone is to berate them, to tell them off harshly.

clue.text: Putting 'oly man's robe on Miller's son, over the top

indicators.note: putting one piece on another in an across clue sets it in front

parts.note: a holy man's robe is a habit; 'oly drops the H, so the robe word loses its H too
Much the Miller's Son is one of Robin Hood's Merry Men

explanation.surface: Dressing Robin Hood's man in a monk's robe, said in a dropped-H accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'oly signals HABIT losing its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is 'a bit much' means it is excessive or overdone.

clue.text: Creator of Earth in gospel (right at the end)

indicators.note: in means the earth letter goes inside
at the end says the right letter is shifted to the finish of the gospel name

parts.note: Mark is one of the four gospels

explanation.surface: God, the creator of the world, described in a gospel, with a bracketed aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker is one who makes, and the Maker is a name for God as creator.

clue.text: Vegetable giving brother internal pain, starting with back

indicators.note: starting with back means the last letter of the pain word moves to the front

parts.note: colic is abdominal pain

explanation.surface: A vegetable that gives a sibling stomach ache, beginning with backache.
explanation.definitionFit: Broccoli is a green vegetable of the cabbage family with edible flower heads.

clue.text: Inappropriate salute to monarch results in enslavement

parts.note: yo is a casual greeting, unsuitable for addressing royalty
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: Greeting the king too casually leads to being enslaved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yo, king' is the inappropriate salute itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoking means harnessing like oxen, so figuratively bringing into subjugation.

clue.text: Offer to take care of former partner first

indicators.note: first says the former partner piece leads

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to tend is to look after

explanation.surface: An offer to look after one's former spouse before anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend an invitation or help is to offer it.

clue.text: Trot oddly up against a wealthy comrade

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the word Trot

parts.note: up against means versus, abbreviated V
wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: A strangely-behaving Trotskyist confronts a rich comrade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trot' suggests a Trotskyist, fitting the Russian answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tovarich is the Russian word for comrade, used between Soviet citizens.
